RADMOR is synonymous with reliable communication and secure data transfer on the modern battlefield, which is a key element of success for every military mission. As a technological leader in innovation, RADMOR has been supporting the defense sector for over 70 years by providing world-class advanced VHF FM mobile radio communication equipment.

The company's flagship products are specialist military radios for tactical communication manufactured by the experienced RADMOR engineering team, which have been successfully used for years by the armed forces of Poland and other countries such as the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Algeria, Nigeria, Malaysia, Morocco, Bangladesh, Indonesia and others. RADMOR also supplies mobile radio sets for armored patrol cars, handheld devices and civilian radios, including TETRA and DMR digital communication systems. The company is also involved in a number of European research programs.

One of them is the ESSOR (European Secure Software Defined Radio) program, which aims to develop a standard for European programmable radio, enabling cooperation between military communication systems of different EU countries. Thanks to its participation in the program, RADMOR has knowledge and experience in implementing and using the ESSOR HDR waveform, as well as SDR platforms. This has enabled the design and production of modern Polish military radios, ensuring the highest level of security of transmitted information. Solutions designed by RADMOR are used not only in the defense sector - the company flexibly adapts to market needs and responds to current customer needs, introducing solutions for the civilian sector to its offer. Among the users of RADMOR's innovative communication and communication tools are also uniformed services, energy, aviation and logistics industries.

Higher education in civil engineering in Romania was founded in 1864, in Bucharest by setting up a "School of Bridges and Roads, Mines and Architecture" which, in 1867 became the "School of Bridges, Roads and Mines" and "the National School for Bridges and Roads" in 1888. In 1921, the "National School of Bridges and Roads" became the "Polytechnic School of Bucharest", where the engineers' training was carried out in the Engineering Department which, in 1938, came to be known as the Faculty of Civil Engineering. 
In 1948, following an Education Reform, the Faculty of Civil Engineering was separated from the Polytechnic School (which became the Polytechnic Institute) and became an independent higher education institution, called the Civil Engineering Institute of Bucharest. Starting with the academic year 1994-1995, the Civil Engineering Institute of Bucharest became The Technical University of Civil Engineering of Bucharest.

Mission & Vision
Immersea Srl is a pioneering technology company specializing in thedigitalization of marine environments and submerged cultural heritage. Through innovative solutions, the company aims toenhance accessibility to underwater ecosystems, making them more understandable and immersive for the public, researchers, and stakeholders.
Core Business Areas
Immersea Srl operates in multiple technological domains, including:
- Marine Environmental Monitoring– Development of cutting-edge solutions for underwater biodiversity assessment, including e-DNA detection systems.

- Submerged Cultural Heritage Digitalization– Creation of 3D models and immersive experiences for archaeological sites and marine protected areas.

- Advanced Visualization Technologies– Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) applications for museums, tourism, and scientific dissemination.

- Remote Sensing & Mapping– Integration of underwater optical mapping and Earth Observation (EO) data for high-precision environmental assessments.

- Scientific Research & Innovation– Collaboration with universities and research institutions to drive technological advancements in marine science.

Key Technologies & Innovations
- e-DNA Sampling & Analysis: Development of filters applicable to DPV/ROV systems for direct in-situ water sampling.

- 3D Underwater Mapping: Optical imaging and digital reconstruction of submerged environments.

- Telemetry & Positioning (Dead Reckoning): Precision tracking of data collection points.

- Data Management Software: AI-driven tools for cataloging and interpreting marine biodiversity data.

- Integration with Space Technologies: Use of satellite imagery and Earth Observation for validation of environmental claims.

Strategic Goals
Immersea aims to bridge the gap betweenscientific research, environmental conservation, and public engagement, leveragingcutting-edge marine and space technologies. By integrating in-situ data collection with remote sensing, Immersea aspires to set new standards inmarine monitoring, environmental certification, and cultural heritage preservation.
